In this case, if $F$ is moreover a morphism of sites $({\cal D}, K)\to ({\cal C}, J)$, the morphisms $C_{F}$ and $\Sh(F)$ realize the topos $\Sh({\cal D}, K)$ as a (coadjoint\footnote{Recall that a retract $(i, r)$ in a $2$-category (in the sense of section B1.1 of \cite{El}), where $r\circ i\cong 1$, is said to be \emph{coadjoint} if $i$ is left adjoint to $r$.}) retract of $\Sh({\cal C}, J)$ in the $2$-category $\mathfrak{Btop}$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: For a continuous comorphism of sites, $C_{F}$ is essential with $(C_{F})_{!}\cong \Sh(F)^{\ast}$; $\Sh(F)$ and $C_{F}$ are adjoint, $\Sh(F)$ is local iff $F$ is $K$-full and $K$-faithful, in which case $\Sh({\cal D},K)$ is a coadjoint retract of $\Sh({\cal C},J)$.
assumptions: Let $F:{\cal D}\to {\cal C}$ be a continuous comorphism of sites (also regarded as a weak morphism of sites) $({\cal D}, K)\to ({\cal C}, J)$
conclusions: The geometric morphism $C_{F}:\Sh({\cal D}, K)\to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$ is essential, and \[ (C_{F})_{!}\cong \Sh(F)^{\ast} \dashv \Sh(F)_{\ast}\cong (C_{F})^{\ast}=D_{F}:=(-\circ F^{\textup{op}}) \dashv (C_{F})_{\ast} \]
The weak morphism $\Sh(F):\Sh({\cal C}, J) \to \Sh({\cal D}, K)$ is local if and only if $C_{F}$ is an inclusion, that is, if and only if $F$ is $K$-faithful and $K$-full.

nodes.name: Subobjects of a sheafification as $c_J$-closed subobjects
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site. Then for any object $F$ of $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]$, denoting by $\textup{ClSub}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]}(F)$ the sub-lattice of $\Sub_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]}(F)$ consisting of the $c_J$-closed subobjects, we have a lattice isomorphism \[ \Sub_{\Sh({\cal C}, J)}(a_{J}(F))\simeq \textup{ClSub}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]}(F) \] which sends a subobject in $\textup{ClSub}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]}(F)$ to its image under $a_{J}$ and a subobject of $a_{J}(F)$ to the pullback of it under the unit arrow $F\to a_{J}(F)$.
nodes.statement_short: Subobjects of $a_J(F)$ in $\Sh({\cal C},J)$ correspond, as a lattice isomorphism, to the $c_J$-closed subobjects of the presheaf $F$.
assumptions: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site
for any object $F$ of $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]$
conclusions: we have a lattice isomorphism \[ \Sub_{\Sh({\cal C}, J)}(a_{J}(F))\simeq \textup{ClSub}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]}(F) \]

nodes.name: Local representation of arrows $l(c)\to l(d)$
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site. \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item Then for any arrow $\xi:l(c)\to l(d)$ in $\Sh({\cal C}, J)$ there exists a family of arrows $\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c, g_{u}:c_{u}\to d \mid u\in U\}$ such that $\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c \mid u\in U\}$ generates a $J$-covering sieve, for any object $e$ and arrows $h:e\to c_{u}$ and $k:e\to c_{u'}$ such that $f_{u}\circ h=f_{u'}\circ k$ we have $g_{u}\circ h\equiv_{J} g_{u'}\circ k$, and $\xi \circ l(f_{u})=l(g_{u})$ for every $u\in U$. \item Conversely, any family of arrows ${\cal F}:\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c, g_{u}:c_{u}\to d \mid u\in U\}$ such that $\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c \mid u\in U\}$ generates a $J$-covering sieve and for any object $e$ and arrows $h:e\to c_{u}$ and $k:e\to c_{u'}$ such that $f_{u}\circ h=f_{u'}\circ k$ we have $g_{u}\circ h\equiv_{J} g_{u'}\circ k$, determines a unique arrow $\xi_{\cal F}:l(c)\to l(d)$ in $\Sh({\cal C}, J)$ such that $\xi_{\cal F}\circ l(f_{u})=l(g_{u})$ for every $u\in U$. \item Two families ${\cal F}=\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c, g_{u}:c_{u}\to d \mid u\in U\}$ and ${\cal F}'=\{f'_{v}:e_{v}\to c, g'_{v}:e_{v}\to d \mid v\in V\}$ as in (ii) determine the same arrow $l(c)\to l(d)$ (i.e. $\xi_{\cal F}=\xi_{{\cal F}'}$) if and only if there exist a $J$-covering family $\{a_{k}:b_{k}\to c \mid k\in K\}$ and factorizations of it through both of them by arrows $x_{k}:b_{k}\to c_{u(k)}$ and $y_{k}:b_{k}\to e_{v(k)}$ (i.e. $f_{u(k)}\circ x_{k}=a_{k}=f'_{v(k)}\circ y_{k}$ for every $k\in K$) such that $g_{u(k)}\circ x_{k}\equiv_{J} g'_{v(k)}\circ y_{k}$ for every $k\in K$. \item Given two families ${\cal F}=\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c, g_{u}:c_{u}\to d \mid u\in U\}$ and ${\cal G}=\{h_{v}:d_{v}\to d, k_{v}:d_{v}\to e \mid v\in V\}$, the composite arrow $\xi_{\cal G}\circ \xi_{\cal F}:l(c)\to l(e)$ is induced as in (ii) by the family $\{f_{u}\circ x:\textup{dom}(x)\to c, k_{v}\circ y:\textup{dom}(y)\to e \mid (u,v,x,y )\in Z\}$, where $Z=\{(u, v, x, y) \mid u\in U, v\in V, \textup{dom}(x)=\textup{dom}(y), \textup{cod}(x)=c_{u}, \textup{cod}(y)=d_{v}, h_{v}\circ y=g_{u}\circ x\}$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: 2.3 Site-theoretic description of arrows between objects coming from the site
nodes.statement_short: Arrows $l(c)\to l(d)$ in $\Sh({\cal C},J)$ are exactly the $J$-locally matching families $\{(f_u,g_u)\}$, up to common refinement, with composition given explicitly.
assumptions: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site
conclusions: for any arrow $\xi:l(c)\to l(d)$ in $\Sh({\cal C}, J)$ there exists a family of arrows $\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c, g_{u}:c_{u}\to d \mid u\in U\}$
any family of arrows ${\cal F}:\{f_{u}:c_{u}\to c, g_{u}:c_{u}\to d \mid u\in U\}$ ... determines a unique arrow $\xi_{\cal F}:l(c)\to l(d)$ in $\Sh({\cal C}, J)$

nodes.name: Existence of an arrow $\xi:l(e)\to l(d)$ with $\xi\circ l(h)=l(k)$
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site and $h:c\to d, k:c\to e$ arrows in $\cal C$. Then there exists an arrow $\xi:l(e)\to l(d)$ such that $\xi \circ l(h)=l(k)$ if and only if there exists a family of arrows $g_{f}:\textup{dom}(f)\to d$ indexed by the arrows $f$ of a $J$-covering sieve $S$ on $e$ such that $g_{f\circ z}=g_{f}\circ z$ whenever $z$ is composable with $f$, and such that for any $\chi\in h^{\ast}(S)$, $k\circ \chi\equiv_{J} g_{h\circ \chi}$.
nodes.section: 2.3 Site-theoretic description of arrows between objects coming from the site
nodes.statement_short: Solvability of $\xi\circ l(h)=l(k)$ is equivalent to an explicit $J$-local matching-family condition on $h$ and $k$.
assumptions: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site
$h:c\to d, k:c\to e$ arrows in $\cal C$
conclusions: there exists an arrow $\xi:l(e)\to l(d)$ such that $\xi \circ l(h)=l(k)$ if and only if there exists a family of arrows $g_{f}:\textup{dom}(f)\to d$ indexed by the arrows $f$ of a $J$-covering sieve $S$ on $e$

nodes.name: Arrows over $l(c)$ coming from the site are epimorphic
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site and $\xi:A\to l(c)$ an arrow of $\Sh({\cal C}, J)$. Then the family of arrows $\chi:l(d)\to A$, where $d\in {\cal C}$, such that $\xi \circ \chi=l(f)$ for some arrow $f:d\to c$ in $\cal C$ is epimorphic on $A$.
nodes.section: 2.3 Site-theoretic description of arrows between objects coming from the site
nodes.statement_short: Any $A\to l(c)$ is covered by arrows $l(d)\to A$ whose composite with it comes from the site.
assumptions: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site
$\xi:A\to l(c)$ an arrow of $\Sh({\cal C}, J)$
conclusions: the family of arrows $\chi:l(d)\to A$, where $d\in {\cal C}$, such that $\xi \circ \chi=l(f)$ for some arrow $f:d\to c$ in $\cal C$ is epimorphic on $A$

nodes.name: $J$-functional relations as $J$-locally pointed functorial assignments
nodes.statement: We have a natural bijection between the $J$-functional relations $R$ from $P$ to $Q$ and the functions $f$ assigning to each element $x\in P(c)$ a $\equiv_{J}$-equivalence class of elements of $Q(c)$ (that is, a subset $A$ of $Q(c)$ such that for any $y\in A$ and $y'\in Q(c)$, $y\equiv_{J} y'$ if and only if $y'\in A$) which is \emph{functorial} in the sense that for any arrow $g:d\to c$ in $\cal C$, if $y\in f(x)$ then $Q(g)(y)\in f(P(g)(x))$, \emph{$J$-closed} in the sense that if $Q(g)(y)\in f(P(g)(x))$ for all the arrows $g$ of a $J$-covering sieve then $y\in f(x)$ and \emph{$J$-locally pointed} in the sense that for any $x\in P(c)$, $\{g:d\to c \mid f(P(g)(x))\neq \emptyset \}\in J(c)$. This correspondence sends \begin{itemize} \item a function $f$ satisfying the above properties to the relation $R_{f}\mono P\times Q$ consisting of the pairs $(x, y)$ such that $y\in f(x)$; \item a $J$-functional relation $R$ from $P$ to $Q$ to the function $f_{R}$ given by: \[ f_{R}(x)=\{y\in Q(c) \mid (x, y)\in R(c)\} \] for any $x\in P(c)$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: $J$-functional relations from $P$ to $Q$ correspond bijectively to functorial, $J$-closed, $J$-locally pointed assignments of $\equiv_J$-classes.
conclusions: We have a natural bijection between the $J$-functional relations $R$ from $P$ to $Q$ and the functions $f$ assigning to each element $x\in P(c)$ a $\equiv_{J}$-equivalence class of elements of $Q(c)$

nodes.name: Monomorphisms and epimorphisms induced by a $J$-functional relation
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a $J$-functional relation from $P$ to $Q$ in $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]$ and $\alpha_{R}:a_{J}(P)\to a_{J}(Q)$ the arrow in $\Sh({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $R$. Then \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item $\alpha_{R}$ is a monomorphism if and only if for any $c\in {\cal C}$ and any elements $(x,y), (x',y')\in R(c)$ such that $y=y'$, the sieve $\{f:d\to c \mid P(f)(x)=P(f)(x')\}$ is $J$-covering. \item $\alpha_{R}$ is an epimorphism if and only if for any $c\in {\cal C}$ and $y\in Q(c)$, the sieve $\{f:d\to c \mid (\exists x\in P(d))((x, Q(f)(y))\in R(d))\}$ is $J$-covering. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Explicit $J$-covering criteria on $R$ for $\alpha_R$ to be monic, resp. epic.
assumptions: Let $R$ be a $J$-functional relation from $P$ to $Q$ in $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]$ and $\alpha_{R}:a_{J}(P)\to a_{J}(Q)$ the arrow in $\Sh({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $R$
conclusions: $\alpha_{R}$ is a monomorphism if and only if for any $c\in {\cal C}$ and any elements $(x,y), (x',y')\in R(c)$ such that $y=y'$, the sieve $\{f:d\to c \mid P(f)(x)=P(f)(x')\}$ is $J$-covering
$\alpha_{R}$ is an epimorphism if and only if for any $c\in {\cal C}$ and $y\in Q(c)$, the sieve $\{f:d\to c \mid (\exists x\in P(d))((x, Q(f)(y))\in R(d))\}$ is $J$-covering

nodes.name: Description of the elements of $a_{J}(P)(c)$
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site. Then \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item An arrow $\xi:l(c)\to a_{J}(P)$ in $\Sh({\cal C}, J)$ (equivalently, an element of $a_{J}(P)(c)$) can be identified with an equivalence class of families $\{x_{f}\in P(\textup{dom}(f)) \mid f\in S\}$ of elements of $P$ indexed by the arrows $f$ of a $J$-covering sieve $S$ on $c$ which are \emph{locally matching} in the sense that for any arrow $g$ composable with an arrow $f\in S$, $x_{f\circ g}\equiv_{J} P(g)(x_{f})$, modulo the equivalence which identifies two such families when they are locally equal on a common refinement. \item Any such family yields a local representation of $\xi$ in the sense that $\xi\circ l(f)=r_{x_{f}}$ for each $f\in S$, where $r_{x_{f}}$ is the image under $a_{J}$ of the arrow $y_{\cal C}(\textup{dom}(f))\to P$ corresponding to the element $x_{f}\in P(\textup{dom}(f))$ via the Yoneda lemma. \item Alternatively, the elements of $a_{J}(P)(c)$ can be identified with functions sending to each arrow $f:d\to c$ in $\cal C$ a (possibly empty) $\equiv_{J}$-equivalence class $C_{f}\subseteq P(\textup{dom}(f))$ of elements of $P(\textup{dom}(f))$ in such a way that \begin{itemize} \item for any $g$ composable with $f$, $P(g)(C_{f})\subseteq C_{f\circ g}$; \item for any $y\in P(\textup{dom}(f))$, if $\{g:\textup{dom}(g)\to \textup{dom}(f) \mid P(g)(y)\in C_{f\circ g}\}\in J(\textup{dom}(f))$ then $y\in C_{f}$; \item $\{g:\textup{dom}(g)\to \textup{dom}(f) \mid C_{f\circ g}\neq \emptyset \}\in J(\textup{dom}(f))$. \end{itemize} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: An element of $a_J(P)(c)$ is a locally matching family of elements of $P$ over a $J$-covering sieve, modulo local equality; equivalently a $J$-closed assignment of $\equiv_J$-classes.
assumptions: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site
conclusions: An arrow $\xi:l(c)\to a_{J}(P)$ in $\Sh({\cal C}, J)$ (equivalently, an element of $a_{J}(P)(c)$) can be identified with an equivalence class of families $\{x_{f}\in P(\textup{dom}(f)) \mid f\in S\}$

nodes.name: Cofinality conditions for $a_{J}(\tilde{\alpha})$ to be an isomorphism
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site and $F:{\cal A}\to {\cal C}$ and $F':{\cal A}'\to {\cal C}$ two functors to $\cal C$ related by a functor $\xi:{\cal A}\to {\cal A}'$ and a natural transformation $\alpha:F\to F'\circ \xi$. Then the canonical arrow \[ \tilde{\alpha}: \textup{colim}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]}(y_{\cal C}\circ F) \to \textup{colim}_{[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]}(y_{\cal C}\circ F') \] defined above is sent by $a_{J}$ to an isomorphism \[ a_{J}(\tilde{\alpha}): \textup{colim}_{\Sh({\cal C}, J)}(l\circ F) \to \textup{colim}_{\Sh({\cal C}, J)}(l\circ F) \] if and only if $(\xi, \alpha)$ satisfies the following \ac cofinality' conditions: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item For any object $c$ of $\cal C$ and any arrow $y:c\to F'(a')$ in $\cal C$ there are a $J$-covering family $\{f_i: c_i \to c \mid i\in I\}$ and for each $i\in I$ an object $a_{i}$ of $\cal A$ and an arrow $y_i:c_{i}\to F(a_{i})$ such that $(y\circ f_{i}, \alpha(a_{i})\circ y_{i})\in R'_{c_{i}}$. \item For any object $c$ of $\cal C$ and any arrows $x:c\to F(a)$ and $x':c\to F(b)$ in $\cal C$ such that $(\alpha(a)\circ x, \alpha(b)\circ x')\in R'_{c}$ there is a $J$-covering family $\{f_i: c_i \to c \mid i\in I\}$ such that $(x\circ f_i, x'\circ f_i)\in R_{c_{i}}$ for each $i\in I$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: The canonical arrow between the two colimits becomes invertible in $\Sh({\cal C},J)$ exactly when $(\xi,\alpha)$ satisfies two explicit $J$-local `cofinality' conditions.
assumptions: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site and $F:{\cal A}\to {\cal C}$ and $F':{\cal A}'\to {\cal C}$ two functors to $\cal C$ related by a functor $\xi:{\cal A}\to {\cal A}'$ and a natural transformation $\alpha:F\to F'\circ \xi$
conclusions: the canonical arrow ... is sent by $a_{J}$ to an isomorphism ... if and only if $(\xi, \alpha)$ satisfies the following \ac cofinality' conditions

nodes.name: $J$-cofinality and the cofinality conditions along a continuous functor
nodes.statement: Let $A:{\cal A}\to {\cal C}$ be a functor and $v:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal C}', J')$ a continuous functor (that is, a weak morphism of sites). If $A$ is $J$-cofinal then it satisfies, together with the identical natural transformation on $v\circ F$, the conditions of Proposition \ref{procofinality}. Moreover, the converse holds if $\Sh(v)^{\ast}$ reflects isomorphisms.
nodes.statement_short: A $J$-cofinal functor satisfies the cofinality conditions after composing with any continuous $v$; the converse holds when $\Sh(v)^{\ast}$ reflects isomorphisms.
assumptions: Let $A:{\cal A}\to {\cal C}$ be a functor and $v:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal C}', J')$ a continuous functor (that is, a weak morphism of sites)
If $A$ is $J$-cofinal
conclusions: it satisfies, together with the identical natural transformation on $v\circ F$, the conditions of Proposition \ref{procofinality}
the converse holds if $\Sh(v)^{\ast}$ reflects isomorphisms

nodes.name: Morphisms of sites are insensitive to passing to the generated topology
nodes.statement: Let $J'$ a collection of sieves on a category $\cal C$, and $J$ the Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$ generated by it. Then any morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J')\to ({\cal D}, K)$ is a morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$.
nodes.statement_short: A morphism of sites out of $({\cal C},J')$ is still one out of $({\cal C},J)$ for the topology $J$ generated by $J'$.
assumptions: Let $J'$ a collection of sieves on a category $\cal C$, and $J$ the Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$ generated by it
conclusions: any morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J')\to ({\cal D}, K)$ is a morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$

nodes.name: Recovery of $K$ from $J$ for a continuous comorphism of sites
nodes.statement: Let $i$ be a $K$-full and $K$-faithful $(K, J)$-continuous comorphism of sites $({\cal D}, K)\to ({\cal C}, J)$. Then $K$ can be explicitly characterized in terms of $J$ as follows: for any sieve $T$ on an object $d$ of $\cal D$, $T\in K(d)$ if and only if the morphism $\textup{Lan}_{i^{\textup{op}}}(m_{T})$ is $J$-bicovering, where $m_{T}:T\mono y_{\cal D}(d)$ is the monomorphism in $[{\cal D}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]$ corresponding to the sieve $T$ and $\textup{Lan}_{i^{\textup{op}}}$ is the left Kan extension functor $[{\cal D}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]\to [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]$ along $i^{\textup{op}}$.
nodes.section: 3.3.1 The smallest Grothendieck topology making a functor a comorphism of sites
nodes.statement_short: For a $K$-full, $K$-faithful, continuous comorphism $i$, a sieve is $K$-covering iff its left Kan extension along $i^{\textup{op}}$ is $J$-bicovering.
assumptions: Let $i$ be a $K$-full and $K$-faithful $(K, J)$-continuous comorphism of sites $({\cal D}, K)\to ({\cal C}, J)$
conclusions: for any sieve $T$ on an object $d$ of $\cal D$, $T\in K(d)$ if and only if the morphism $\textup{Lan}_{i^{\textup{op}}}(m_{T})$ is $J$-bicovering

nodes.name: Explicit description of $J\vee R_{i}$
nodes.statement: Let $i$ be a full and faithful functor ${\cal D}\to {\cal C}$ and $J$ a Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$ such that for every $J$-covering sieve $T$ on an object of the form $i(d)$ for $d\in {\cal D}$, $T\cap \textup{Im}(i)\in J(i(d))$. Then the Grothendieck topology $J\vee R_{i}$ admits the following explicit description: for any sieve $T$ on an object $c$ of $\cal C$, $T\in (J\vee R_{i})(c)$ if and only if for every arrow $\xi:i(d)\to c$, $\xi^{\ast}(T)\in J(i(d))$.
nodes.section: 3.3.1 The smallest Grothendieck topology making a functor a comorphism of sites
nodes.statement_short: Under a local-restriction hypothesis, $T$ is $(J\vee R_i)$-covering iff every pullback of $T$ along an arrow out of $i(d)$ is $J$-covering.
assumptions: Let $i$ be a full and faithful functor ${\cal D}\to {\cal C}$ and $J$ a Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$ such that for every $J$-covering sieve $T$ on an object of the form $i(d)$ for $d\in {\cal D}$, $T\cap \textup{Im}(i)\in J(i(d))$
conclusions: for any sieve $T$ on an object $c$ of $\cal C$, $T\in (J\vee R_{i})(c)$ if and only if for every arrow $\xi:i(d)\to c$, $\xi^{\ast}(T)\in J(i(d))$

nodes.name: Adjoint functors, morphisms and comorphisms of sites
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ and $({\cal D}, K)$ be small-generated sites, and $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}\dashv G:{\cal D}\to {\cal C}$ adjoint functors. Then \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item $F$ has the covering-lifting property if and only if $G$ is cover-preserving. \item $G$ is a morphism of sites $({\cal D}, T_{\cal D})\to ({\cal C}, T_{\cal C})$, where $T_{\cal C}$ and $T_{\cal D}$ are the trivial topologies respectively on $\cal C$ and $\cal D$, and induces an essential geometric morphism $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]\to [{\cal D}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]$; \item $G$ is a morphism of sites $({\cal D}, K) \to ({\cal C}, J)$ (equivalently, by (i), $G$ is cover-preserving) if and only if $F$ is a comorphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$. \item In the situation of (iii), the geometric morphism $C_{F}$ induced by $F$ co-incides with the geometric morphism $\Sh(G)$ induced by $G$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: 3.4 Relating morphisms and comorphisms of sites
nodes.statement_short: For $F\dashv G$: $F$ has the covering-lifting property iff $G$ is cover-preserving, and then $C_{F}\cong \Sh(G)$.
assumptions: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ and $({\cal D}, K)$ be small-generated sites, and $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}\dashv G:{\cal D}\to {\cal C}$ adjoint functors
conclusions: $F$ has the covering-lifting property if and only if $G$ is cover-preserving
$G$ is a morphism of sites $({\cal D}, K) \to ({\cal C}, J)$ ... if and only if $F$ is a comorphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$
the geometric morphism $C_{F}$ induced by $F$ co-incides with the geometric morphism $\Sh(G)$ induced by $G$

nodes.name: Relating $M^{F}_{J}$ and $M^{\pi^{F}_{\cal C}}_{J}$
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site and $F:{\cal D}\to {\cal C}$ a functor. Then \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item A sieve $S$ on an object $(c, d, \alpha:c\to F(d))$ of the category is $(1_{\cal C}\downarrow F)$ is $M^{\pi^{F}_{\cal C}}_{J}$-covering if and only if it contains a family of arrows of the form $\{(f_i, 1_{d}):(c_i, d, \alpha:c\to F(d)) \to (c, d, \alpha:c\to F(d))\}$ such that the family $\{f_i:c_i\to c \mid i\in I\}$ is $J$-covering. \item $M^{F}_{J}=M_{M^{\pi_{\cal C}^{F}}_{J}}^{i_{F}'}$. \item $({M^{F}_{J}})^{i_{F}'}=M^{\pi^{F}_{\cal C}}_{J}\vee R_{i_{F}'}$, where $R_{i_{F}'}={T_{\cal C}}^{i_{F}'}$ is the rigid topology associated with the inclusion $i_{F}'$ (here $T_{\cal C}$ denotes the trivial Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$). \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: 3.4.4 The fibration of generalized elements of a functor
nodes.statement_short: Explicit description of the $M^{\pi^{F}_{\cal C}}_{J}$-covering sieves plus the two identities $M^{F}_{J}=M_{M^{\pi_{\cal C}^{F}}_{J}}^{i_{F}'}$ and $({M^{F}_{J}})^{i_{F}'}=M^{\pi^{F}_{\cal C}}_{J}\vee R_{i_{F}'}$.
assumptions: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site and $F:{\cal D}\to {\cal C}$ a functor

nodes.name: $M_{J}^{F}$-covering sieves tested through $i_{F}'$
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site and $F:{\cal D}\to {\cal C}$ a functor. Then, for any sieve $T$ on an object $d$ of $\cal D$, $T$ is $M_{J}^{F}$-covering if and only if it is sent by $i_{F}'$ to a $(M_{J}^{{\pi^{F}_{\cal C}}}\vee R_{i_{F}'})$-covering family.
nodes.section: 3.4.4 The fibration of generalized elements of a functor
nodes.statement_short: $T$ is $M^{F}_{J}$-covering iff $i_{F}'(T)$ is $(M_{J}^{\pi^{F}_{\cal C}}\vee R_{i_{F}'})$-covering.
assumptions: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site and $F:{\cal D}\to {\cal C}$ a functor
conclusions: for any sieve $T$ on an object $d$ of $\cal D$, $T$ is $M_{J}^{F}$-covering if and only if it is sent by $i_{F}'$ to a $(M_{J}^{{\pi^{F}_{\cal C}}}\vee R_{i_{F}'})$-covering family

nodes.name: Faithfulness of a right adjoint vs local surjectivity of its left adjoint
nodes.statement: Let $\cal E$ and $\cal F$ categories and $L\dashv R$ a pair of adjoint functors $R:{\cal E}\to {\cal F}$ and $L:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$. The the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item $R$ is faithful. \item For any $e\in {\cal E}$, there is $u\in {\cal F}$ and an epimorphism $L(u)\to e$. \end{enumerate} If $\cal E$ and $\cal F$ are Grothendieck toposes respectively with separating sets $\cal C$ and $\cal D$ then condition (ii) is equivalent to the following one: for any $c\in {\cal D}$, the family of arrows $L(d)\to c$ (where $d\in {\cal D}$) is epimorphic.
nodes.statement_short: For $L\dashv R$, $R$ is faithful iff every object of $\cal E$ admits an epimorphism from an object in the image of $L$.
assumptions: Let $\cal E$ and $\cal F$ categories and $L\dashv R$ a pair of adjoint functors $R:{\cal E}\to {\cal F}$ and $L:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$
conclusions: $R$ is faithful.
For any $e\in {\cal E}$, there is $u\in {\cal F}$ and an epimorphism $L(u)\to e$.

nodes.name: Weak morphisms factoring through a geometric inclusion
nodes.statement: Let $i:{\cal F}\hookrightarrow {\cal E}$ be the geometric inclusion of a subtopos $\cal F$ of a Grothendieck topos $\cal E$ into $\cal E$, and let $f:{\cal G}\to {\cal E}$ be a weak morphism from a Grothendieck topos $\cal G$. Then the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item The weak morphism $f$ factors through $i$; \item The direct image $f_{\ast}$ takes values in $\cal F$ (that is, factors through $i_{\ast}$); \item The inverse image $f^{\ast}$ factors (necessarily uniquely up to isomorphism) through $i^{\ast}$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: A weak morphism factors through a subtopos inclusion iff its direct image lands in the subtopos, iff its inverse image factors through $i^{\ast}$.
assumptions: Let $i:{\cal F}\hookrightarrow {\cal E}$ be the geometric inclusion of a subtopos $\cal F$ of a Grothendieck topos $\cal E$ into $\cal E$, and let $f:{\cal G}\to {\cal E}$ be a weak morphism from a Grothendieck topos $\cal G$
conclusions: The weak morphism $f$ factors through $i$;
The direct image $f_{\ast}$ takes values in $\cal F$ (that is, factors through $i_{\ast}$);
The inverse image $f^{\ast}$ factors (necessarily uniquely up to isomorphism) through $i^{\ast}$.

nodes.name: $(J, K)$-continuity via $D_{A}$ restricting to sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ and $({\cal D}, K)$ be small-generated sites and $A:{\cal C} \to {\cal D}$ a functor. Then the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item $A$ is $(J, K)$-continuous. \item The functor $$D_{A}:=(-\circ A^{\textup{op}}):[{\cal D}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]\to [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]$$ restricts to a functor $\Sh({\cal D}, K) \to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $A$ is $(J,K)$-continuous iff $-\circ A^{\textup{op}}$ carries $K$-sheaves to $J$-sheaves; this identifies the notion with Grothendieck's continuous functors.
assumptions: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ and $({\cal D}, K)$ be small-generated sites and $A:{\cal C} \to {\cal D}$ a functor
conclusions: $A$ is $(J, K)$-continuous.
The functor $$D_{A}:=(-\circ A^{\textup{op}}):[{\cal D}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]\to [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]$$ restricts to a functor $\Sh({\cal D}, K) \to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$.

nodes.name: Characterizations of $J$-continuous and $(J, K)$-continuous functors
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ and $({\cal D}, K)$ be small-generated sites and $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos. Then \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item A functor $A:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ is $J$-continuous if and only if for any $J$-covering sieve $S$ on an object $c$ \[ A(c)=\varinjlim_{f:d\to c \in S} A(d) \] for each $J$-covering sieve $S$ on an object $c$ (where the colimit is indexed by the category $\int S$ of elements of $S$). \item A functor $A:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ is $(J, K)$-continuous if and only if for any $J$-covering sieve $S$ on an object $c$ the canonical cocone with vertex $A(c)$ on the diagram $\{A(\textup{dom}(f)) \mid f\in S\}$ indexed over $\int S$ is sent by $l'$ to a colimit in the topos $\Sh({\cal D}, K)$. \item Every $J$-continuous functor $A:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ is $J$-continuous in the sense of Definition \ref{defcanonicalfunctor}(a) is $J$-continuous in the sense of section VII.7 of \cite{MM} (that is, sends $J$-covering families to epimorphic families), and the converse is true if $A$ is flat (but not in general, cf. Remark \ref{remflatnessandcanonicity}). More generally, every $(J, K)$-continuous functor $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ is cover-preserving, and every morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ is $(J, K)$-continuous. \item For any functor $A:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$, there is a largest Grothendieck topology $J$ on the category $\cal C$ such that $A$ is $J$-continuous. This topology, denoted by $Z_{A}$, admits the following explicit description: for any sieve $S$ on an object $c$ of $\cal C$, $S$ is $Z_{A}$-covering if and only if for any arrow $g:d\to c$, $A(d)=\varinjlim_{h:e\to d \in g^{\ast}(S)} A(e)$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $J$-continuity means $A(c)=\varinjlim_{f\in S}A(\dom f)$ for every $J$-covering sieve; it implies cover-preservation, and there is a largest such topology $Z_{A}$.
assumptions: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ and $({\cal D}, K)$ be small-generated sites and $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos
conclusions: A functor $A:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ is $J$-continuous if and only if for any $J$-covering sieve $S$ on an object $c$ \[ A(c)=\varinjlim_{f:d\to c \in S} A(d) \]
For any functor $A:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$, there is a largest Grothendieck topology $J$ on the category $\cal C$ such that $A$ is $J$-continuous.

nodes.name: Explicit characterization of $(J, K)$-continuous functors
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ and $({\cal D}, K)$ be small-generated sites. Then a functor $A:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ is $(J, K)$-continuous if and only if it is cover-preserving (i.e., sends $J$-covering families to $K$-covering ones) and for any $J$-covering sieve $S$ on an object $c$ and any commutative square of the form \[ \xymatrix{ d \ar[r] \ar[d] & A(c') \ar[d]^{A(f)} \\ A(c'') \ar[r]^{A(g)} & A(c), } \] where $f:c'\to c$ and $g:c''\to c$ are arbitrary arrows of $S$, there is a $K$-covering family $\{d_{i}\to d \mid i\in I\}$ such that for each $i\in I$, the composites $d_{i}\to A(c')$ and $d_{i}\to A(c'')$ belong to the same connected component of the category $(d_{i}\downarrow D^{A}_{S})$.
nodes.statement_short: $A$ is $(J,K)$-continuous iff it is cover-preserving and every cone over an $S$-square is locally connected in $(d_i\downarrow D^{A}_{S})$.
assumptions: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ and $({\cal D}, K)$ be small-generated sites
conclusions: a functor $A:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ is $(J, K)$-continuous if and only if it is cover-preserving (i.e., sends $J$-covering families to $K$-covering ones) and for any $J$-covering sieve $S$ on an object $c$ and any commutative square ... there is a $K$-covering family $\{d_{i}\to d \mid i\in I\}$ such that for each $i\in I$, the composites $d_{i}\to A(c')$ and $d_{i}\to A(c'')$ belong to the same connected component of the category $(d_{i}\downarrow D^{A}_{S})$

nodes.name: Continuous comorphisms of sites between $M^{A}_{K}$ and $Z_{A}$
nodes.statement: Let $A:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ be a functor and $K$ a Grothendieck topology on $\cal D$. Then for any Grothendieck topology $J$ on $\cal C$ such that $M^{A}_{K}\subseteq J\subseteq Z_{A}$, the functor $A$ is a $(J, K)$-continuous comorphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$. We have $M^{A}_{K}\subseteq Z_{A}$ if and only if for any arrow $g:d\to c$ of $\cal C$ and any $K$-covering sieve $R$ on $A(c)$, \[ A(d)=\varinjlim_{h:e\to d \in g^{\ast}(S^{A}_{R})} A(e). \]
nodes.statement_short: Any topology squeezed between the smallest comorphism topology $M^{A}_{K}$ and the largest continuity topology $Z_{A}$ makes $A$ a continuous comorphism of sites.
assumptions: Let $A:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ be a functor and $K$ a Grothendieck topology on $\cal D$
conclusions: for any Grothendieck topology $J$ on $\cal C$ such that $M^{A}_{K}\subseteq J\subseteq Z_{A}$, the functor $A$ is a $(J, K)$-continuous comorphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$

nodes.name: Weak morphisms to a presheaf or sheaf topos as $J$-continuous functors
nodes.statement: Let $\cal C$ a locally small category and $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos. \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item There is an equivalence \[ \textup{\bf Wmor}({\cal E}, [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set])\simeq [{\cal C}, {\cal E}] \] sending a weak morphism $f=(f^{\ast}\dashv f_{\ast})$ to the functor $f^{\ast}\circ y_{\cal C}$. \item For any Grothendieck topology $J$ on $\cal C$ making $({\cal C}, J)$ a small-generated site, the above equivalence restricts to an equivalence \[ \textup{\bf Wmor}({\cal E}, \Sh({\cal C}, J))\simeq [{\cal C}, {\cal E}]_{J} \] sending a weak morphism $g=(g^{\ast}\dashv g_{\ast})$ to the functor $g^{\ast}\circ l$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $\textup{\bf Wmor}({\cal E},[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}},\Set])\simeq [{\cal C},{\cal E}]$, restricting to $\textup{\bf Wmor}({\cal E},\Sh({\cal C},J))\simeq [{\cal C},{\cal E}]_{J}$.
assumptions: Let $\cal C$ a locally small category and $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos
conclusions: There is an equivalence \[ \textup{\bf Wmor}({\cal E}, [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set])\simeq [{\cal C}, {\cal E}] \] sending a weak morphism $f=(f^{\ast}\dashv f_{\ast})$ to the functor $f^{\ast}\circ y_{\cal C}$.
the above equivalence restricts to an equivalence \[ \textup{\bf Wmor}({\cal E}, \Sh({\cal C}, J))\simeq [{\cal C}, {\cal E}]_{J} \]

nodes.name: Weak morphisms of sites induce weak geometric morphisms
nodes.statement: Any weak morphism $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ of small-generated sites induces a weak geometric morphism $\Sh(F):\Sh({\cal D}, K)\to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$ such that the following diagram commutes: $$ \xymatrix{ {\mathcal C} \ar[r]^F \ar[d]_{l} &{\cal D} \ar[d]^{l'} \\ \Sh({\cal C}, J) \ar[r]^{\Sh(F)^{\ast}} & \Sh({\cal D}, K) } $$ Conversely, any weak geometric morphism $f=(f^{\ast}\dashv f_{\ast})$ such that $f^{\ast}\circ l$ factors through $l'$ is induced by a (necessarily unique, if $K$ is subcanonical) weak morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$.
nodes.statement_short: Weak morphisms of sites correspond to weak geometric morphisms whose inverse image restricted along $l$ factors through $l'$.
conclusions: Any weak morphism $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ of small-generated sites induces a weak geometric morphism $\Sh(F):\Sh({\cal D}, K)\to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$

any weak geometric morphism $f=(f^{\ast}\dashv f_{\ast})$ such that $f^{\ast}\circ l$ factors through $l'$ is induced by a (necessarily unique, if $K$ is subcanonical) weak morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$

nodes.name: Sheafification and composition with $F^{\textup{op}}$
nodes.statement: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a comorphism of sites and $P$ a presheaf on $\cal D$. Then the canonical arrow \[ P\circ F^{\textup{op}} \to a_{K}(P)\circ F^{\textup{op}} \] in $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]$ is sent by the associated sheaf functor $a_{J}:[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set] \to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$ to an isomorphism. If moreover $F$ is $(J, K)$-continuous (for instance, if $F$ is a morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J) \to ({\cal D}, K)$ -- cf. Proposition \ref{propcharJcanonical}(iii)) then the above arrow yields an isomorphism \[ a_{J}(P\circ F^{\textup{op}})\cong a_{K}(P)\circ F^{\textup{op}}. \]
nodes.section: 4.3 Continuous comorphisms of sites and essential geometric morphisms
nodes.statement_short: For a comorphism of sites the unit $P\circ F^{\textup{op}}\to a_{K}(P)\circ F^{\textup{op}}$ is $J$-bicovering, and an isomorphism after $a_J$ when $F$ is continuous.
assumptions: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a comorphism of sites and $P$ a presheaf on $\cal D$
conclusions: the canonical arrow \[ P\circ F^{\textup{op}} \to a_{K}(P)\circ F^{\textup{op}} \] in $[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]$ is sent by the associated sheaf functor $a_{J}:[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set] \to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$ to an isomorphism
the above arrow yields an isomorphism \[ a_{J}(P\circ F^{\textup{op}})\cong a_{K}(P)\circ F^{\textup{op}}. \]

nodes.name: Localization of the geometric morphism induced by a comorphism of sites
nodes.statement: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a comorphism of sites and $Q$ a presheaf on $\cal D$. The geometric morphism \[ C_{p^{F}_{Q}}:\Sh(\textstyle \int (Q\circ F^{\textup{op}}), J_{Q\circ F^{\textup{op}}}) \to \Sh(\textstyle \int Q, J_{Q}) \] induced by $p^{F}_{Q}$ corresponds under the equivalences \[ \Sh({\textstyle \int Q\circ F^{\textup{op}}}, J_{Q\circ F^{\textup{op}}}) \simeq \Sh({\cal C}, J)\slash a_{J}(Q\circ F^{\textup{op}}) \] and \[ \Sh({\textstyle \int Q}, J_{Q}) \simeq \Sh({\cal D}, K) \slash a_{K}(Q) \] of section \ref{sec:example} to the geometric morphism \[ C_{F}\slash a_{K}(Q):\Sh({\cal D}, K)\slash a_{K}(Q) \to \Sh({\cal C}, J)\slash C_{F}^{\ast}(a_{K}(Q)) \] modulo the equivalence \[ \Sh({\cal C}, J)\slash C_{F}^{\ast}(a_{K}(Q))\cong \Sh({\cal C}, J)\slash a_{J}(Q\circ F^{\textup{op}}) \] induced by the isomorphisms \[ C_{F}^{\ast}(a_{K}(Q))\cong a_{K}(Q)\circ F^{\textup{op}}\cong a_{J}(Q\circ F^{\textup{op}}), \] the first of which results from the fact that $F$ is a continuous comorphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ and the second of which is that of Proposition \ref{propcompositionsheafificationcomorphism}.
nodes.section: 4.3 Continuous comorphisms of sites and essential geometric morphisms
nodes.statement_short: $C_{p^{F}_{Q}}$ is, up to the slice equivalences, the localization $C_{F}\slash a_{K}(Q)$ of $C_{F}$.
assumptions: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a comorphism of sites and $Q$ a presheaf on $\cal D$
conclusions: The geometric morphism \[ C_{p^{F}_{Q}}:\Sh(\textstyle \int (Q\circ F^{\textup{op}}), J_{Q\circ F^{\textup{op}}}) \to \Sh(\textstyle \int Q, J_{Q}) \] induced by $p^{F}_{Q}$ corresponds ... to the geometric morphism \[ C_{F}\slash a_{K}(Q):\Sh({\cal D}, K)\slash a_{K}(Q) \to \Sh({\cal C}, J)\slash C_{F}^{\ast}(a_{K}(Q)) \]

nodes.name: Continuity of comorphisms of sites is stable under relativization
nodes.statement: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a $(J, K)$-continuous comorphism of sites. Then, for any presheaf $Q$ on $\cal D$, the comorphism of sites \[ p^{F}_{Q}:(\textstyle \int (Q\circ F^{\textup{op}}), J_{Q\circ F^{\textup{op}}}) \to (\textstyle \int Q, J_{Q}) \] is $(J_{Q\circ F^{\textup{op}}}, J_{Q})$-continuous.
nodes.section: 4.3 Continuous comorphisms of sites and essential geometric morphisms
nodes.statement_short: If $F$ is continuous then so is each relativization $p^{F}_{Q}$ over a presheaf $Q$ on $\cal D$.
assumptions: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a $(J, K)$-continuous comorphism of sites
for any presheaf $Q$ on $\cal D$
conclusions: the comorphism of sites \[ p^{F}_{Q}:(\textstyle \int (Q\circ F^{\textup{op}}), J_{Q\circ F^{\textup{op}}}) \to (\textstyle \int Q, J_{Q}) \] is $(J_{Q\circ F^{\textup{op}}}, J_{Q})$-continuous

nodes.name: Morphisms of sites whose essential image restricts to representables
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C},J)$ and $({\cal D}, K)$ be small-generated subcanonical sites and $g:\Sh({\cal C},J) \to \Sh({\cal D}, K)$ be a geometric morphism induced by a morphism of sites $G:({\cal D}, K) \to ({\cal C},J)$. Then the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item $g$ is essential and its essential image restricts to the representables; \item $G:{\cal D}\to {\cal C}$ has a left adjoint $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ which is $(J, K)$-continuous. \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: 4.3 Continuous comorphisms of sites and essential geometric morphisms
nodes.statement_short: $g=\Sh(G)$ is essential with essential image restricting to representables iff $G$ has a $(J,K)$-continuous left adjoint.
assumptions: Let $({\cal C},J)$ and $({\cal D}, K)$ be small-generated subcanonical sites and $g:\Sh({\cal C},J) \to \Sh({\cal D}, K)$ be a geometric morphism induced by a morphism of sites $G:({\cal D}, K) \to ({\cal C},J)$
conclusions: $g$ is essential and its essential image restricts to the representables;
$G:{\cal D}\to {\cal C}$ has a left adjoint $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ which is $(J, K)$-continuous.

nodes.name: Cofinality conditions transported along a continuous comorphism
nodes.statement: Let $p:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a continuous comorphism of small-generated sites such that $(C_{p})_{!}$ is conservative, and $F:{\cal A}\to {\cal C}$ and $F:{\cal A}'\to {\cal C}$ two functors to $\cal C$ related by a functor $\xi:{\cal A}\to {\cal A}'$ and a natural transformation $\alpha:F\to F'\circ \xi$. Then $(\xi, \alpha)$ satisfies the conditions of Proposition \ref{procofinality} if and only if $(\xi, p\alpha)$ does.
nodes.section: 4.3 Continuous comorphisms of sites and essential geometric morphisms
nodes.statement_short: If $(C_p)_!$ is conservative, $(\xi,\alpha)$ satisfies the cofinality conditions iff $(\xi,p\alpha)$ does.
assumptions: Let $p:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a continuous comorphism of small-generated sites such that $(C_{p})_{!}$ is conservative
conclusions: $(\xi, \alpha)$ satisfies the conditions of Proposition \ref{procofinality} if and only if $(\xi, p\alpha)$ does

nodes.name: Essential images preserve $P$-compact objects
nodes.statement: Let $P$ be a stable property of presieves and let $f$ be an essential geometric morphism. Then $f_{!}$ sends $P$-compact objects to $P$-compact objects.
nodes.statement_short: For a stable property $P$ of presieves, $f_{!}$ sends $P$-compact objects to $P$-compact objects.
assumptions: Let $P$ be a stable property of presieves and let $f$ be an essential geometric morphism
conclusions: $f_{!}$ sends $P$-compact objects to $P$-compact objects

nodes.name: Intrinsic description of the topology $J^{c}_{P}$ on $P$-compact objects
nodes.statement: Let $P$ be a property of presieves in a topos, $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos and ${\cal E}^{c}_{P}$ the full subcategory of $\cal E$ on the $P$-compact objects. Suppose that \begin{enumerate}[(1)] \item ${\cal E}^{c}_{P}$ is separating for $\cal E$, \item $P$ is fractal and relativizes to separating sets (or at least to the separating set ${\cal E}^{c}_{P}$ of $\cal E$), \item for any effective-epimorphic family ${\cal R}=\{r_i:\dom(r_i) \to c \mid i\in I\}$ in ${\cal E}^{c}_{P}$ satisfying $P|_{{\cal E}^{c}_{P}}$, the family of canonical colimit arrows $\{\lambda_i:\dom(r_i) \to e \mid i\in I\}$, where $e$ is the colimit of the diagram $D_{{\cal R}}$ in $\cal E$, also satisfies $P$. \end{enumerate} Then the Grothendieck topology $J^{c}_{P}$ on ${\cal E}^{c}_{P}$ induced by the canonical topology on $\cal E$ can be intrinsically characterized (in terms of ${\cal E}^{c}_{P}$) as follows: the $J^{c}_{P}$-covering sieves on an object $c$ of ${\cal E}^{c}_{P}$ are precisely those which contain a family of arrows to $c$ which satisfies $P|_{{\cal E}^{c}_{P}}$ and is effective-epimorphic (equivalently, universally effective-epimorphic). Conditions (2) and (3) can be replaced by the following condition: \begin{enumerate} \item[(4)] The category ${\cal E}^{c}_{P}$ is closed in $\cal E$ under colimits of diagrams of the form $D_{\cal R}$, where $\cal R$ is an effective-epimorphic family of arrows in ${\cal E}^{c}_{P}$ satisfying $P|_{{\cal E}^{c}_{P}}$. \end{enumerate} which in fact implies (3), and is implied by (3) assuming (1) and (2). Condition (3) is satisfied if $P$ is stable under pullback and hereditary.
nodes.statement_short: Under fractality/relativization hypotheses, the induced topology on ${\cal E}^{c}_{P}$ has as covers the sieves containing an effective-epimorphic family satisfying $P$.

nodes.name: Weakly essential geometric morphisms and complete frame homomorphisms
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item Every essential geometric morphism $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$ is weakly essential; in fact, more generally, all the frame homomorphisms of the form $f^{\ast}|_{\Sub_{\cal E}(A)}:\Sub_{\cal E}(A) \to \Sub_{\cal F}(f^{\ast}(A))$, where $A$ is an object of $A$, are complete (equivalently, they admit a left adjoint). \item For any locales $L$ and $L'$, the weakly essential geometric morphisms $\Sh(L)\to \Sh(L')$ correspond precisely to the complete frame homomorphisms $L'\to L$. \item Let $u:L'\to L$ be a complete locale homomorphism whose corresponding geometric morphism $\Sh(u):\Sh(L')\to \Sh(L)$ is essential. Then the left adjoint to the frame homomorphism associated with $u$ does not in general take the same values as the restriction of the essential image of $\Sh(u)$ to the subterminal objects of $\Sh(L)$. \item There are weakly essential morphisms between localic toposes which are not essential; in other words, the property of a frame homomorphism being complete is a necessary but not sufficient condition for the associated geometric morphism to be essential. \item Any weakly essential morphism between toposes which can be represented as the toposes of presheaves on some posets is essential. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Essential implies weakly essential; weakly essential localic morphisms are exactly the complete frame homomorphisms, and completeness is not sufficient for essentialness.
conclusions: Every essential geometric morphism $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$ is weakly essential
For any locales $L$ and $L'$, the weakly essential geometric morphisms $\Sh(L)\to \Sh(L')$ correspond precisely to the complete frame homomorphisms $L'\to L$.
There are weakly essential morphisms between localic toposes which are not essential

nodes.name: Presheaf lifting of a comorphism of sites
nodes.statement: Any comorphism of sites $f:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal C}', J')$ extends to a comorphism of sites $\hat{f}:([{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set], \hat{J}) \to ([{\cal C}'^{\textup{op}}, \Set], \hat{J'})$ given by the left Kan extension along $f^{\textup{op}}$, and the following diagram commutes: \[ \xymatrix{ \Sh({\cal C}, J) \ar[r] \ar[d]_{C_{f}} & \Sh([{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set], \hat{J}) \ar[d]^{C_{\hat{f}}} \\ \Sh({\cal C}', J') \ar[r] & \Sh([{{\cal C}'}^{\textup{op}}, \Set], \hat{J'}) } \]
nodes.statement_short: Every comorphism of sites extends, via left Kan extension, to a comorphism between the presheaf sites $(\hat{\cal C},\hat J)$.
assumptions: Any comorphism of sites $f:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal C}', J')$
conclusions: extends to a comorphism of sites $\hat{f}:([{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set], \hat{J}) \to ([{\cal C}'^{\textup{op}}, \Set], \hat{J'})$ given by the left Kan extension along $f^{\textup{op}}$

nodes.name: The Yoneda embedding as a bimorphism of sites
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site. Then the Yoneda embedding $y_{\cal C}:{\cal C}\to [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]$ is both a morphism and a comorphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to (\hat{\cal C}, \hat{J})$. It is moreover $\hat{J}$-dense (and $J$-full), so (cf. Proposition \ref{propmorphismcomorphismequivalence}) it induces an equivalence of toposes \[ \Sh({\cal C}, J) \simeq \Sh(\hat{\cal C}, \hat{J}) \] one half of which is $C_{y_{\cal C}}$ and whose other half is $\Sh(y_{\cal C})$.
nodes.statement_short: $y_{\cal C}:({\cal C},J)\to (\hat{\cal C},\hat J)$ is both a morphism and a comorphism of sites and induces the equivalence $\Sh({\cal C},J)\simeq \Sh(\hat{\cal C},\hat J)$.
assumptions: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site
conclusions: the Yoneda embedding $y_{\cal C}:{\cal C}\to [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]$ is both a morphism and a comorphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to (\hat{\cal C}, \hat{J})$
it induces an equivalence of toposes \[ \Sh({\cal C}, J) \simeq \Sh(\hat{\cal C}, \hat{J}) \]

nodes.name: Lifting continuity along a fibration
nodes.statement: Let $A:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$, $B:({\cal C}, J) \to ({\cal E}, L)$ and $C:({\cal D}, K)\to ({\cal E}, L)$ be comorphisms of sites related by a natural isomorphism $C\circ A\cong B$. If $B$ is $(J, L)$-continuous and $C$ is a fibration then $A$ satisfies the conditions of Proposition \ref{propcharcanonicalfunctors} with respect to every $J$-covering sieve $S$ which satisfies the property that there is a functorial factorization $g=g_{c}\circ g_{v}$ for any arrow $g$ in $S$ such that $g_{c}$ lies in $S$, $A(g_{c})$ is a cartesian arrow and $A(g_{v})$ is a vertical arrow (whence the factorization $A(g)=A(g_{c})\circ A(g_{v})$ yields \ac the' decomposition of $A(g)$ in $\cal D$ as a vertical arrow followed by a cartesian arrow); that is, for any such sieve $S$ on an object $c$, $A(S)$ is $K$-covering and for any commutative square of the form \[ \xymatrix{ d \ar[r] \ar[d] & A(c') \ar[d]^{A(f)} \\ A(c'') \ar[r]^{A(g)} & A(c), } \] where $f:c'\to c$ and $g:c''\to c$ are arbitrary arrows of $S$, there is a $K$-covering family $\{d_{i}\to d \mid i\in I\}$ such that for each $i\in I$, the composites $d_{i}\to A(c')$ and $d_{i}\to A(c'')$ belong to the same connected component of the category $(d_{i}\downarrow D^{A}_{S})$.
nodes.statement_short: If $C\circ A\cong B$ with $B$ continuous and $C$ a fibration, then $A$ satisfies the continuity conditions with respect to every sieve admitting a functorial cartesian/vertical factorization.
assumptions: Let $A:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$, $B:({\cal C}, J) \to ({\cal E}, L)$ and $C:({\cal D}, K)\to ({\cal E}, L)$ be comorphisms of sites related by a natural isomorphism $C\circ A\cong B$
If $B$ is $(J, L)$-continuous and $C$ is a fibration
conclusions: $A$ satisfies the conditions of Proposition \ref{propcharcanonicalfunctors} with respect to every $J$-covering sieve $S$ which satisfies the property that there is a functorial factorization $g=g_{c}\circ g_{v}$ for any arrow $g$ in $S$

nodes.name: Cartesian images along a morphism of fibrations
nodes.statement: Let $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ and $G:{\cal D}\to {\cal E}$ be fibrations and $H$ a morphism of fibrations $F\to G$. Then $H$ satisfies the following property: for any object $c$ of $\cal C$ and arrow $g:d\to H(c)$ in $\cal D$, there is a cartesian (with respect to $F$) arrow $f:c'\to c$ and a vertical arrow $v:d'\to H(c')$ such that $g=H(f)\circ v$ (note that $H(f)$ is cartesian with respect to $G$ since $f$ is cartesian and $H$ is a morphism of fibrations). In other words, the cartesian image of an arrow towards an object in the image of $H$ also lies in the image of $H$.
nodes.statement_short: For a morphism of fibrations $H$, the cartesian image of an arrow into the image of $H$ again lies in the image of $H$.
assumptions: Let $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ and $G:{\cal D}\to {\cal E}$ be fibrations and $H$ a morphism of fibrations $F\to G$
conclusions: for any object $c$ of $\cal C$ and arrow $g:d\to H(c)$ in $\cal D$, there is a cartesian (with respect to $F$) arrow $f:c'\to c$ and a vertical arrow $v:d'\to H(c')$ such that $g=H(f)\circ v$

nodes.name: Reduction of the condition $\Gamma^{f}_{h}$ along epimorphic families
nodes.statement: Let $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$ be an essential geometric morphism between Grothendieck toposes and $h:A\to B$ an arrow of $\cal E$. \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item For any epimorphic family $\{f_{i}:A_{i}\to A \mid i\in I\}$ in $\cal E$, $\Gamma^{f}_{h}$ holds if and only if $\Gamma^{f}_{h\circ f_{i}}$ holds for every $i\in I$. \item For any epimorphic family $\{g_{j}:B_{j}\to B \mid j\in J\}$ in $\cal E$, $\Gamma^{f}_{h}$ holds if and only if $\Gamma^{f}_{g_{j}^{\ast}(h)}$ holds for every $j\in J$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $\Gamma^{f}_{h}$ may be tested on a covering family of the domain or on the pullbacks along a covering family of the codomain.
assumptions: Let $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$ be an essential geometric morphism between Grothendieck toposes and $h:A\to B$ an arrow of $\cal E$
conclusions: For any epimorphic family $\{f_{i}:A_{i}\to A \mid i\in I\}$ in $\cal E$, $\Gamma^{f}_{h}$ holds if and only if $\Gamma^{f}_{h\circ f_{i}}$ holds for every $i\in I$.
For any epimorphic family $\{g_{j}:B_{j}\to B \mid j\in J\}$ in $\cal E$, $\Gamma^{f}_{h}$ holds if and only if $\Gamma^{f}_{g_{j}^{\ast}(h)}$ holds for every $j\in J$.

nodes.name: Terminally connected morphisms are orthogonal to local homeomorphisms
nodes.statement: Terminally connected morphisms are orthogonal to local homeomorphisms in the $2$-category of Grothendieck toposes; that is, for any commutative square \begin{equation*} \begin{tikzcd} {\cal F} \arrow[rr, "f"] \arrow[d, "m"] & & {\cal E} \arrow[d, "n"] \arrow[dll, dashed, "k"{above}] \\ {\cal G} \ar[rr, "g"] & & {\cal H}, \end{tikzcd} \end{equation*} where $f$ is terminally connected and $g$ is a local homeomorphism, there exists a morphism $k:{\cal E}\to {\cal G}$ (unique up to unique $2$-isomorphism) making both triangles commute.
nodes.statement_short: Any commutative square with a terminally connected morphism on one side and a local homeomorphism on the other admits a unique diagonal filler.
assumptions: for any commutative square ... where $f$ is terminally connected and $g$ is a local homeomorphism
conclusions: there exists a morphism $k:{\cal E}\to {\cal G}$ (unique up to unique $2$-isomorphism) making both triangles commute

nodes.name: Terminally connected--local homeomorphism factorization
nodes.statement: Any essential geometric morphism can be factored, uniquely up to equivalence, as a terminally connected morphism followed by a local homeomorphism. In particular, an essential geometric morphism $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$ factors as a terminally connected morphism $f':{\cal F}\to {\cal E}\slash f_{!}(1)$ followed by the canonical local homeomorphism $U_{f_{!}(1)}:{\cal E}\slash f_{!}(1) \to {\cal E}$.
nodes.statement_short: Every essential geometric morphism factors uniquely as a terminally connected morphism followed by the local homeomorphism $U_{f_{!}(1)}$.
conclusions: Any essential geometric morphism can be factored, uniquely up to equivalence, as a terminally connected morphism followed by a local homeomorphism.

an essential geometric morphism $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$ factors as a terminally connected morphism $f':{\cal F}\to {\cal E}\slash f_{!}(1)$ followed by the canonical local homeomorphism $U_{f_{!}(1)}:{\cal E}\slash f_{!}(1) \to {\cal E}$

nodes.name: Terminal connectedness of $C_{F}$ and $K$-cofinality of $F$
nodes.statement: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a continuous comorphism of small-generated sites. Then the geometric morphism $C_{F}:\Sh({\cal C}, J)\to \Sh({\cal D}, K)$ induced by $F$ is terminally connected (resp. connected and locally connected) if and only if $F$ is $K$-cofinal (resp. $F$ is $K$-cofinal and satisfies the conditions of Theorem \ref{thmlocallyconnected}).
nodes.statement_short: For a continuous comorphism, $C_{F}$ is terminally connected exactly when $F$ is $K$-cofinal.
assumptions: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a continuous comorphism of small-generated sites
conclusions: the geometric morphism $C_{F}:\Sh({\cal C}, J)\to \Sh({\cal D}, K)$ induced by $F$ is terminally connected (resp. connected and locally connected) if and only if $F$ is $K$-cofinal (resp. $F$ is $K$-cofinal and satisfies the conditions of Theorem \ref{thmlocallyconnected})

nodes.name: Adjunction between $\Sh({\cal C}, J)$ and $\textup{\bf Cat}\slash\slash {\cal C}$
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site. Then the functors \[ U:\Sh({\cal C}, J)\to \textup{\bf Cat}\slash\slash {\cal C} \] and \[ V:\textup{\bf Cat}\slash\slash {\cal C} \to \Sh({\cal C}, J) \] which send respectively a $J$-sheaf $P$ on $\cal C$ to the associated discrete fibration $$\pi_{P}:{\textstyle \int P}\to {\cal C}$$ and a functor $F:{\cal A}\to {\cal C}$ to the $K$-sheaf $$F_{K}:=\textup{colim}_{\Sh({\cal C}, J)}(l_{\cal C}\circ F)$$ on $\cal D$ (and act on arrows in the obvious way) are adjoint to each other ($U$ on the right and $V$ on the left), and this adjunction restricts to an equivalence between $\Sh({\cal C}, J)$ and the full subcategory of $\textup{\bf Cat} \slash\slash {\cal C}$ on the discrete $J$-glueing fibrations.
nodes.statement_short: $V\dashv U$ between sheaves and functors over $\cal C$, restricting to an equivalence with the discrete $J$-glueing fibrations.
assumptions: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site
conclusions: are adjoint to each other ($U$ on the right and $V$ on the left)
this adjunction restricts to an equivalence between $\Sh({\cal C}, J)$ and the full subcategory of $\textup{\bf Cat} \slash\slash {\cal C}$ on the discrete $J$-glueing fibrations

nodes.name: Orthogonality of cofinal functors to glueing discrete fibrations
nodes.statement: The following orthogonality property of cofinal functors with respect of glueing fibrations (along continuous functors) holds: for any commutative square \begin{equation*} \begin{tikzcd} {\cal A} \arrow[rr, "F"] \arrow[d, "u"] & & {\cal C} \arrow[d, "v"] \arrow[dll, dashed, "G"{above}] \\ {\cal B} \ar[rr, "p"] & & {\cal C}' \end{tikzcd} \end{equation*} where $\cal C$ and ${\cal C}'$ are respectively endowed with Grothendieck topologies $J$ and $J'$ such that $v$ is $(J, J')$-continuous, $F$ is $J$-cofinal and $p$ is a $J'$-glueing discrete fibration, there is a unique (up to isomorphism) functor $G:{\cal C}\to {\cal B}$ which makes both triangles commute (up to isomorphism).
nodes.statement_short: A $J$-cofinal functor is orthogonal to a $J'$-glueing discrete fibration along a continuous functor: the diagonal filler exists and is unique up to isomorphism.
assumptions: for any commutative square ... where $\cal C$ and ${\cal C}'$ are respectively endowed with Grothendieck topologies $J$ and $J'$ such that $v$ is $(J, J')$-continuous, $F$ is $J$-cofinal and $p$ is a $J'$-glueing discrete fibration
conclusions: there is a unique (up to isomorphism) functor $G:{\cal C}\to {\cal B}$ which makes both triangles commute (up to isomorphism)

nodes.name: Characterization of the $K$-comprehensive factorization
nodes.statement: Let $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ be a functor and $K$ a Grothendieck topology on $\cal D$. \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item The $K$-comprehensive factorization of $F$ is characterized by being the unique (up to equivalence) factorization of $F$ as a $M^{p}_{K}$-cofinal functor ${\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ followed by a $K$-glueing fibration $p:{\cal E}\to {\cal D}$. \item If $F$ is a continuous comorphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ then $\xi^{F}_{K}:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\int F_{K}}, M^{\pi_{F_{K}}}_{K})$ and $F_{K}:({\int F_{K}}, M^{\pi_{F_{K}}}_{K}) \to ({\cal D}, K)$ are continuous comorphism of sites and $C_{F}\cong C_{F_{K}}\circ C_{\xi^{F}_{K}}$ is the terminally connected-local homeomorphism factorization of the geometric morphism $C_{F}:\Sh({\cal C}, J)\to \Sh({\cal D}, K)$ (cf. Proposition \ref{propfactorizationdiscrete}). \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: The $K$-comprehensive factorization is the unique factorization into a cofinal functor followed by a $K$-glueing fibration, and realizes the terminally connected--local homeomorphism factorization of $C_{F}$.
assumptions: Let $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ be a functor and $K$ a Grothendieck topology on $\cal D$
conclusions: The $K$-comprehensive factorization of $F$ is characterized by being the unique (up to equivalence) factorization of $F$ as a $M^{p}_{K}$-cofinal functor ${\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ followed by a $K$-glueing fibration $p:{\cal E}\to {\cal D}$.
$C_{F}\cong C_{F_{K}}\circ C_{\xi^{F}_{K}}$ is the terminally connected-local homeomorphism factorization of the geometric morphism $C_{F}:\Sh({\cal C}, J)\to \Sh({\cal D}, K)$

nodes.name: Equivalence implies density for a morphism into a subcanonical site
nodes.statement: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of sites. Suppose that $K$ is subcanonical. Then, if the geometric morphism $\Sh(F):\Sh({\cal D}, K)\to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$ is an equivalence, $F$ is a dense morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$.
nodes.section: 5 Denseness conditions and equivalences of toposes
nodes.statement_short: If $K$ is subcanonical and $\Sh(F)$ is an equivalence, then $F$ is a dense morphism of sites.
assumptions: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of sites
Suppose that $K$ is subcanonical
conclusions: if the geometric morphism $\Sh(F):\Sh({\cal D}, K)\to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$ is an equivalence, $F$ is a dense morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$

nodes.name: Explicit characterization of weakly dense morphisms of sites
nodes.statement: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of sites. Then $F$ is a weakly dense morphism of sites if and only if it satisfies the following conditions: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item $P$ is a $J$-covering family in $\cal C$ if and only if $F(P)$ is a $K$-covering family in $\cal D$; \item for any object $d$ of $\cal D$ there exist a family $\{S_{i} \mid i\in I\}$ of $K$-covering sieves on objects of the form $F(c_{i})$ (where $c_{i}$ is an object of $\cal C$) and for each $f\in S_{i}$ an arrow $g_{f}:\textup{dom}(f)\to d$ such that $g_{f\circ z}\equiv_{K} g_{f}\circ z$ whenever $z$ is composable with $f$, such that the family of arrows $g_{f}$ (for $f\in S_{i}$ for some $i$) is $K$-covering; \item for any objects $x, y$ of ${\cal C}$ and any family of arrows $g_{h}:\textup{dom}(h)\to F(y)$ indexed by the arrows of a $K$-covering sieve $U$ on $F(x)$ such that $g_{h\circ k}\equiv_{K} g_{h}\circ k$ for every arrow $k$ composable with $h$, there exist a $J$-covering family of arrows $\{f_{i}:x_{i}\to x \mid i\in I\}$ and arrows $k_{i}:x_{i}\to y$ (for each $i\in I$) such that for every arrows $w$ and $z$ such that $F(f_{i})\circ w=h\circ z$, we have $g_{h}\circ z\equiv_{K} F(k_{i})\circ w$ (for every $h\in U$ and $i\in I$). \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Three explicit conditions -- cover-reflection, local covering by images, and local fullness up to $\equiv_K$ -- characterize weak density.
assumptions: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of sites
conclusions: $F$ is a weakly dense morphism of sites if and only if it satisfies the following conditions

nodes.name: $J$-fullness and $J$-faithfulness via the canonical arrow into $a_J(\textup{Hom}(F(-),F(c)))$
nodes.statement: Let $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ be a functor and $J$ a Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$. Then $F$ is $J$-full and $J$-faithful if and only if for any $c\in {\cal C}$, the canonical arrow $l(c)\to a_{J}(\textup{Hom}_{\cal D}(F(-), F(c)))$ is an isomorphism in $\Sh({\cal C}, J)$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Local faithfulness, local fullness and local surjectivity
nodes.statement_short: $F$ is $J$-full and $J$-faithful iff $l(c)\to a_{J}(\textup{Hom}_{\cal D}(F(-), F(c)))$ is an isomorphism for every $c$.
assumptions: Let $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ be a functor and $J$ a Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$
conclusions: $F$ is $J$-full and $J$-faithful if and only if for any $c\in {\cal C}$, the canonical arrow $l(c)\to a_{J}(\textup{Hom}_{\cal D}(F(-), F(c)))$ is an isomorphism in $\Sh({\cal C}, J)$

nodes.name: Dense morphisms of sites have the covering-lifting property
nodes.statement: Let $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ be a $J$-full, $K$-dense, cover-reflecting and cover-preserving functor (for instance, a dense morphism of sites $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$). Then $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ has the covering-lifting property.
nodes.section: 5.3 Local faithfulness, local fullness and local surjectivity
nodes.statement_short: $J$-full + $K$-dense + cover-reflecting + cover-preserving implies the covering-lifting property.
assumptions: Let $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ be a $J$-full, $K$-dense, cover-reflecting and cover-preserving functor (for instance, a dense morphism of sites $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$)
conclusions: $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ has the covering-lifting property

nodes.name: Local properties of $F$ versus properties of $a_{F}$
nodes.statement: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of sites. Then \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item $F$ is $(J, K)$-faithful if and only if $a_{F}$ is faithful; \item If $F$ is $(J, K)$-faithful and satisfies the covering-lifting property then $F$ is $(J, K)$-full if and only if $a_{F}$ is full; \item If $F$ satisfies the covering-lifting property then $F$ is $K$-dense if and only if $a_{F}$ is $C^{\cal D}_{K}$-dense. \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: 5.3 Local faithfulness, local fullness and local surjectivity
nodes.statement_short: $(J,K)$-faithfulness/fullness/$K$-density of $F$ correspond to faithfulness/fullness/density of the induced functor $a_{F}$.
assumptions: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of sites
conclusions: $F$ is $(J, K)$-faithful if and only if $a_{F}$ is faithful;
If $F$ is $(J, K)$-faithful and satisfies the covering-lifting property then $F$ is $(J, K)$-full if and only if $a_{F}$ is full;
If $F$ satisfies the covering-lifting property then $F$ is $K$-dense if and only if $a_{F}$ is $C^{\cal D}_{K}$-dense.

nodes.name: Surjections and cover-reflecting continuous flat functors
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site, $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos and $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ a $J$-continuous flat functor. Then the geometric morphism $f:{\cal E}\to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ is a surjection (that is, $f^{\ast}$ is faithful) if and only if $F$ is \emph{cover-reflecting} (in the sense that the $J$-covering families in $\cal C$ are precisely those which are sent by $F$ to epimorphic families in $\cal E$).
nodes.statement_short: $f$ is a surjection iff the $J$-covering families are exactly those sent by $F$ to epimorphic families.
assumptions: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site, $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos and $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ a $J$-continuous flat functor
conclusions: the geometric morphism $f:{\cal E}\to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ is a surjection (that is, $f^{\ast}$ is faithful) if and only if $F$ is \emph{cover-reflecting}

nodes.name: Grothendieck topology induced by a geometric morphism or a flat functor
nodes.statement: Let $f:{\cal E}\to [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]$ be a geometric morphism (equivalently, a flat functor $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$). Then there exists a Grothendieck topology $J_{f}$ (resp. $J_{F}$) on $\cal C$, called the Grothendieck topology \emph{induced} by $f$ (resp. $F$) whose covering sieves are precisely the sieves which are sent by $f^{\ast}$ (resp. by $F$) to epimorphic families in $\cal E$. This applies in particular to a morphism of small-generated sites $G:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$, yielding a Grothendieck topology $J_{G}$ on $\cal C$ whose covering sieves are exactly those whose image under $G$ are $K$-covering families (cf. Theorem \ref{Morphismsmaalgenerated}(ii)).
nodes.statement_short: Every flat functor / geometric morphism induces a topology $J_{F}$ whose covers are the sieves sent to epimorphic families.
assumptions: Let $f:{\cal E}\to [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]$ be a geometric morphism (equivalently, a flat functor $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$)
conclusions: there exists a Grothendieck topology $J_{f}$ (resp. $J_{F}$) on $\cal C$, called the Grothendieck topology \emph{induced} by $f$ (resp. $F$) whose covering sieves are precisely the sieves which are sent by $f^{\ast}$ (resp. by $F$) to epimorphic families in $\cal E$

nodes.name: Recovery of $K$ from $J$ for a $K$-dense covering-lifting functor
nodes.statement: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a $K$-dense functor with the covering-lifting property (for instance, a dense morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ -- cf. Corollary \ref{corequivalencecovliftproperty}). Then the Grothendieck topology $K$ can be recovered from $J$, as follows: for any sieve $T$ on an object $d$ of $\cal D$, $T\in K(d)$ if and only if for any object $c\in {\cal C}$ and any arrow $\xi:F(c)\to d$ in $\cal D$, there exists a $J$-covering sieve $R$ on $c$ such that $F(R)\subseteq \xi^{\ast}(T)$.
nodes.statement_short: $T$ is $K$-covering iff every pullback of $T$ along an arrow out of $F(c)$ contains the image of a $J$-covering sieve.
assumptions: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a $K$-dense functor with the covering-lifting property
conclusions: for any sieve $T$ on an object $d$ of $\cal D$, $T\in K(d)$ if and only if for any object $c\in {\cal C}$ and any arrow $\xi:F(c)\to d$ in $\cal D$, there exists a $J$-covering sieve $R$ on $c$ such that $F(R)\subseteq \xi^{\ast}(T)$

nodes.name: A general setup for building equivalences of toposes
nodes.statement: Let $\cal E$ be a Grothendieck topos, represented as the category $\Sh({\cal D}, K)$ of sheaves on a small-generated site $({\cal D}, K)$. Let $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ be a functor and $J_{F}$ the collection of sieves in $\cal C$ whose image under $F$ is $K$-covering. If $F$ is a weakly dense morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J_{F})\to ({\cal D}, K)$ then $J_{F}$ is a Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$, and we have an equivalence of toposes \[ \Sh({\cal D}, K) \simeq \Sh({\cal C}, J_{F}). \] The following conditions are equivalent to $F$ being a dense (or weakly dense, if $K$ is subcanonical) morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J_{F})\to ({\cal D}, K)$: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item[(i)'] For any object $d$ of $\cal D$ there exists a $K$-covering family of arrows $d_{i}\to d$ whose domains $d_{i}$ are in the image of $F$. \item[(ii)'] For every $c_{1}, c_{2}\in {\cal C}$ and any arrow $g:F(c_{1})\to F(c_{2})$ in $\cal D$, there exist a family of arrows $f_{i}:c'_{i}\to c_{1}$ which is sent by $F$ to a $K$-covering family and a family of arrows $k_{i}:c'_{i}\to c_{2}$ such that $g\circ F(f_{i})=F(k_{i})$ for all $i$. \item[(iii)'] For any arrows $f_{1}, f_{2}:c_{1}\to c_{2}$ in $\cal C$ such that $F(f_1)=F(f_2)$ there exists a family of arrows $k_{i}:c'_{i}\to c_{1}$ which is sent by $F$ to a $K$-covering family such that $f_1 \circ k_{i}=f_{2}\circ k_{i}$ for all $i$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: If $F$ is a weakly dense morphism of sites for the collection $J_{F}$, then $J_{F}$ is a topology and $\Sh({\cal D},K)\simeq \Sh({\cal C},J_{F})$.
assumptions: Let $\cal E$ be a Grothendieck topos, represented as the category $\Sh({\cal D}, K)$ of sheaves on a small-generated site $({\cal D}, K)$
Let $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ be a functor and $J_{F}$ the collection of sieves in $\cal C$ whose image under $F$ is $K$-covering
If $F$ is a weakly dense morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J_{F})\to ({\cal D}, K)$
conclusions: $J_{F}$ is a Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$, and we have an equivalence of toposes \[ \Sh({\cal D}, K) \simeq \Sh({\cal C}, J_{F}). \]

nodes.name: Image (coinduced) topology $J^{F}$ of a Grothendieck topology along a functor
nodes.statement: Let $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ be a functor and $J$ a Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$. Then there is a Grothendieck topology $J^{F}$ on $\cal D$, called the \emph{image of $J$ along $F$} (or the Grothendieck topology \emph{coinduced} by $J$ along $F$), such that for any sieve $T$ on an object $d$ of $\cal D$, $T\in J^{F}(d)$ if and only if for any object $c\in {\cal C}$ and any arrow $\xi:F(c)\to d$ in $\cal D$, there exists a $J$-covering sieve $R$ on $c$ such that $F(R)\subseteq \xi^{\ast}(T)$. Then the functor $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, J^{F})$ is $J^{F}$-dense and has the covering-lifting property. The Grothendieck topology $J^{F}$ enjoys the following universal property: the subtopos $\Sh({\cal D}, J^{F})\hookrightarrow [{\cal D}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]$ is the image (in the sense of surjection-inclusion factorization) of the composite of the induced geometric morphism $[F^{\textup{op}}, \Set]:[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]\to [{\cal D}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]$ with the subtopos inclusion $\Sh({\cal C}, J)\hookrightarrow [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, \Set]$.
nodes.origin_citation: Johnstone, Sketches of an Elephant, Lemma C2.3.19(ii)
nodes.statement_short: There is a largest topology $J^{F}$ on $\cal D$ making $F$ covering-lifting; $\Sh({\cal D},J^{F})$ is the image of the induced geometric morphism.
assumptions: Let $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ be a functor and $J$ a Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$
conclusions: there is a Grothendieck topology $J^{F}$ on $\cal D$, called the \emph{image of $J$ along $F$} (or the Grothendieck topology \emph{coinduced} by $J$ along $F$)
the functor $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, J^{F})$ is $J^{F}$-dense and has the covering-lifting property

nodes.name: Closure of the image of $f^{\ast}$ under subobjects tested on a separating set
nodes.statement: Let ${\cal C}$ be a separating set for a Grothendieck topos $\cal E$ and $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$ a geometric morphism. Then the image of $f^{\ast}$ is closed under subobjects if and only if for any $c\in {\cal C}$, every subobject of $f^{\ast}(c)$ is in the image of $f^{\ast}$.
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to check closure under subobjects on the objects $f^{\ast}(c)$ for $c$ in a separating set.
assumptions: Let ${\cal C}$ be a separating set for a Grothendieck topos $\cal E$ and $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$ a geometric morphism
conclusions: the image of $f^{\ast}$ is closed under subobjects if and only if for any $c\in {\cal C}$, every subobject of $f^{\ast}(c)$ is in the image of $f^{\ast}$

nodes.name: Hyperconnectedness for continuous flat functors
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site, $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos and $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ a $J$-continuous flat functor. Then the geometric morphism $f:{\cal E}\to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ is hyperconnected if and only if $F$ is cover-reflecting and for every subobject $A\mono F(c)$ in $\cal E$ there exists a ($J$-closed) sieve $R$ on $c$ such that $A$ is the union of the images of the arrows $F(f)$ for $f\in R$.
nodes.statement_short: $f$ is hyperconnected iff $F$ is cover-reflecting and every subobject of $F(c)$ is a union of images of arrows $F(f)$, $f$ in a $J$-closed sieve.
assumptions: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site, $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos and $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ a $J$-continuous flat functor
conclusions: the geometric morphism $f:{\cal E}\to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ is hyperconnected if and only if $F$ is cover-reflecting and for every subobject $A\mono F(c)$ in $\cal E$ there exists a ($J$-closed) sieve $R$ on $c$ such that $A$ is the union of the images of the arrows $F(f)$ for $f\in R$

nodes.name: Hyperconnectedness for morphisms of sites: closed-sieve-lifting
nodes.statement: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of small-generated sites. Then the geometric morphism $\Sh(F):\Sh({\cal D}, K) \to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ is hyperconnected if and only if $F$ is cover-reflecting and \emph{closed-sieve-lifting}, in the sense that for every object $c$ of $\cal C$ and any $K$-closed sieve $S$ on $F(c)$ there exists a ($J$-closed) sieve $R$ on $c$ such that $S$ coincides with the ($K$-closed) sieve on $F(c)$ generated by the arrows $F(f)$ for $f\in R$.
nodes.statement_short: $\Sh(F)$ is hyperconnected iff $F$ is cover-reflecting and closed-sieve-lifting.
assumptions: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of small-generated sites
conclusions: the geometric morphism $\Sh(F):\Sh({\cal D}, K) \to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ is hyperconnected if and only if $F$ is cover-reflecting and \emph{closed-sieve-lifting}

nodes.name: Essential surjectivity of $f^{\ast}$ and separating families
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site, $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos and $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ a $J$-continuous flat functor inducing a geometric morphism $f:{\cal E}\to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$. If the image of $f^{\ast}$ is closed under subobjects then $f^{\ast}$ is essentially surjective if and only if the objects of the form $F(c)$ for $c\in {\cal C}$ form a separating set for the topos $\cal E$.
nodes.statement_short: When the image of $f^{\ast}$ is closed under subobjects, $f^{\ast}$ is essentially surjective iff the $F(c)$ form a separating set.
assumptions: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site, $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos and $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ a $J$-continuous flat functor inducing a geometric morphism $f:{\cal E}\to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$
If the image of $f^{\ast}$ is closed under subobjects
conclusions: $f^{\ast}$ is essentially surjective if and only if the objects of the form $F(c)$ for $c\in {\cal C}$ form a separating set for the topos $\cal E$

nodes.name: Essential surjectivity for morphisms of sites
nodes.statement: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of small-generated sites. Then the geometric morphism $\Sh(F):\Sh({\cal D}, K) \to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ satisfies the property that $\Sh(F)^{\ast}$ is essentially surjective and its image is closed under subobjects if and only if $F$ is closed-sieve-lifting (in the sense of Proposition \ref{prophyperconnectedsites}) and satisfies condition (ii) of Proposition \ref{propweaklydensemorphism} (equivalently, if $K$ is subcanonical, every object of $\cal D$ admits a $K$-covering sieve generated by arrows whose domain lies in the image of $F$).
nodes.statement_short: $\Sh(F)^{\ast}$ is essentially surjective with image closed under subobjects iff $F$ is closed-sieve-lifting and satisfies the local covering condition (ii).
assumptions: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of small-generated sites
conclusions: the geometric morphism $\Sh(F):\Sh({\cal D}, K) \to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ satisfies the property that $\Sh(F)^{\ast}$ is essentially surjective and its image is closed under subobjects if and only if $F$ is closed-sieve-lifting ... and satisfies condition (ii) of Proposition \ref{propweaklydensemorphism}

nodes.name: Localic morphisms and separating sets
nodes.statement: Let ${\cal C}$ (resp. $\cal D$) be a separating set for a Grothendieck topos $\cal E$ (resp. $\cal F$) and $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$ a geometric morphism. Then: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item The full subcategory $\cal G$ of $\cal F$ on the objects which are subquotients of objects of the form $f^{\ast}(A)$ for $A\in {\cal E}$ coincides with the full subcategory of $\cal F$ on the objects which can be covered by objects which are domains of subobjects of objects of the form $f^{\ast}(A)$ for $A$ in $\cal C$. \item $f$ is localic if and only if every object of $\cal D$ can be covered by objects which are domains of subobjects of objects of the form $f^{\ast}(A)$ for $A$ in $\cal C$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Subquotients of objects $f^{\ast}(A)$ are exactly the objects covered by subobjects of $f^{\ast}(A)$ with $A$ in a separating set; localicness is testable on a separating set of $\cal F$.
assumptions: Let ${\cal C}$ (resp. $\cal D$) be a separating set for a Grothendieck topos $\cal E$ (resp. $\cal F$) and $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$ a geometric morphism
conclusions: $f$ is localic if and only if every object of $\cal D$ can be covered by objects which are domains of subobjects of objects of the form $f^{\ast}(A)$ for $A$ in $\cal C$

nodes.name: Localic morphisms for continuous flat functors
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site, $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos and $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ a $J$-continuous flat functor inducing a geometric morphism $f:{\cal E}\to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$. Then $f$ is localic if and only if the subobjects of objects of the form $F(c)$ for $c\in {\cal C}$ form a separating set for the topos $\cal E$.
nodes.statement_short: $f$ is localic iff the subobjects of the $F(c)$ form a separating set for $\cal E$.
assumptions: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site, $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos and $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ a $J$-continuous flat functor inducing a geometric morphism $f:{\cal E}\to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$
conclusions: $f$ is localic if and only if the subobjects of objects of the form $F(c)$ for $c\in {\cal C}$ form a separating set for the topos $\cal E$

nodes.name: Localic morphisms for morphisms of sites
nodes.statement: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of small-generated sites. Then the geometric morphism $\Sh(F):\Sh({\cal D}, K) \to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ is localic if and only if for any object $d$ of $\cal D$ there exist a family $\{S_{i} \mid i\in I\}$ of sieves on objects of the form $F(c_{i})$ (where $c_{i}$ is an object of $\cal C$) and for each $f\in S_{i}$ an arrow $g_{f}:\textup{dom}(f)\to d$ such that $g_{f\circ z}\equiv_{K} g_{f}\circ z$ whenever $z$ is composable with $f$, such that the family of arrows $g_{f}$ (for $f\in S_{i}$ for some $i$) is $K$-covering.
nodes.statement_short: $\Sh(F)$ is localic iff every object of $\cal D$ is $K$-covered by locally matching families indexed by sieves on objects $F(c_i)$.
assumptions: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of small-generated sites
conclusions: the geometric morphism $\Sh(F):\Sh({\cal D}, K) \to \Sh({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ is localic if and only if for any object $d$ of $\cal D$ there exist a family $\{S_{i} \mid i\in I\}$ of sieves on objects of the form $F(c_{i})$ ... such that the family of arrows $g_{f}$ ... is $K$-covering

nodes.name: Interpretations inducing a localic geometric morphism
nodes.statement: Let $I:{\cal C}_{\mathbb T}\to {\cal C}_{\mathbb S}$ be an interpretation of a geometric theory $\mathbb T$ into a geometric theory ${\mathbb S}$.
